date_tested: 1995 (start date UNKNOWN; claimed in the 1995-10-04 release)

cost_or_effort: Free editorial nomination; submission effort and criteria UNKNOWN
result: COMPANY SELF-REPORT ONLY: the release states Amazon was included and that this was 'effectively trumpeting its arrival to any user who clicks the button to see the list'. No dated third-party listing for amazon.com survives, and no order attribution exists
repeatability: UNKNOWN: directory inclusion depended on editorial discretion, not on a purchasable process
notes: Do NOT label this viral or organic: it is earned editorial placement asserted by the company about itself. The NCSA Mosaic August-1995 'What's New' archive (3,084 entries) is in-window but contains the river, not the company.

date_tested: 1995 (start date UNKNOWN; claimed in the 1995-10-04 release)
why_tested: Same: the dominant consumer route to new sites in 1995
result: COMPANY SELF-REPORT ONLY, same single sentence as the Netscape claim; no independent listing dated inside the window survives

channel: Own press release distributed by wire

result: Reproduced by at least one wire reprint (URLwire item 100495) and echoed in period features by November 1995; conversion UNKNOWN
repeatability: Partly: the company issued releases on a cadence thereafter, but the 1995-10-04 text survives only as a summarised extract (restoration pending)
confidence: High that issued / Medium that distributed / UNKNOWN effect
notes: This one document is the ancestor of the titles, discount, shipping, geography, channel-listing, phone-number, review and Bezos-quotation claims: nine claims, ONE source.

why_tested: Not chosen by the company: third parties described the live store
result: Two dated outside descriptions of the store exist, one of them syndicated nationally, and both mention ordering by Web, toll-free phone or fax
repeatability: UNKNOWN: earned coverage cannot be scheduled; neither item reports an order
notes: Both reach us via a 2019 aggregator reprint; the print originals are not held (RD-011). A High-confidence validation signal cannot rest on a reprint.

date_tested: 1995-10-04 ('share their thoughts ... exchange ideas'), with user postings quoted in the release
why_tested: To turn a thin, technical audience into content that improved the catalogue for others
result: The company quoted real user postings in its own release, including a warning about overspending; volume UNKNOWN. The origin of the first reviews ('employees and friends wrote them') is a 2025-sourced claim
notes: Do not describe this as a UGC flywheel: no 1995 volume, cadence or effect is measured anywhere.

channel: Personal network and invited beta list
date_tested: ~1995-05 (six-week closed beta, per retrospective accounts); claimed first outside order 1995-04-03
why_tested: Prove the order-to-card path before the public site existed
cost_or_effort: Founder and employee time; ~300 invited users
result: The one documented converted buyer of the period exists because an employee e-mailed a friend to create an account and order books; every element of that account is 2012-2015 retrospective
repeatability: One-time by nature: a personal network cannot be re-tested at scale
notes: FOUNDER CLAIM / retrospective telling (Sheff 1999/2000; Kaphan 2011; MarketWatch 2015). Tension with the audited 'no sales through July 1995' is unresolved (U.1).

channel: Published telephone number and toll-free ordering line
date_tested: 1995-10-04 (the number is published in the release); the toll-free line is the S-1's own disclosure (S-1 (orig.) l.2179-2180); offline ordering attested by 1995-11
why_tested: To take orders from buyers unwilling to type a card number on the Web
cost_or_effort: Telephony and manual order entry; cost UNKNOWN
result: The toll-free line was maintained specifically for customers refusing online card entry, and card details could be given by e-mail or telephone; orders by fax are attested only by the Nov-1995 press; share of orders taken this way UNKNOWN
notes: A trust device, not an acquisition channel: it converted demand that had already arrived. COR-13 attribution: the 1995-10-04 release (S1701) supplies the published number and online ordering ONLY — it names no toll-free line, no mailbox count, no fax and no e-mail ordering, so it is NOT the source of this row's substance; nine addresses at S-1 (orig.) l.2174. The Nov-1995 fax detail rests on Knight Ridder (S0612) and the incomplete reprint chain (RD-011).

why_tested: The available route to a dispersed technical audience before search was mature
result: Positive customer reviews circulating in chat groups were reported to have driven some visitors; no measurement of any kind
notes: Reported retrospectively by a newspaper in 1997, not measured in 1995. Word of mouth was never measured in Stage 1 at all.

why_tested: Discovery as the Web outgrew directories
result: NOT EVIDENCED for 1995: two unnamed 'key search engines' surfaced Amazon 'early on' per 1997 reporting, and a claim that 1995 traffic came from search engines failed tracing
notes: Recorded as an unsupported channel so it is not quietly credited to Stage 1 (G-33). The 1995 offer itself was search-led, which is a product feature, not an acquisition channel.

channel: Physical gifts sent to the customer base
date_tested: undated: 'in the past sent' per the March-1997 filing
why_tested: Retention, as the company describes it
cost_or_effort: Cost, date, volume and result all UNKNOWN
result: No evidence that this channel operated inside Stage 1; the disclosure is a 1997 statement in undated past tense
notes: Kept in the register as an un-dated claim, not as a Stage-1 experiment (D-72). No 1995 gift cost or order effect exists.

channel: Word of mouth as a growth theory
why_tested: The company's stated model was that satisfied customers tell others across a network with near-zero marginal reach cost
cost_or_effort: $30,000 of FY1995 advertising against $200,000 of marketing and sales: paid acquisition was near-absent
result: ASSERTED, NEVER MEASURED: the filing's word-of-mouth sentence is a theory filed under penalty of perjury, not a metric; referral share of 1995 orders is UNKNOWN
repeatability: Not testable on the surviving record
confidence: High (that the company said it) / UNKNOWN (that it worked)
notes: The honest Stage-1 statement is: with almost no paid media, orders arrived - the mechanism is unidentified. 'Viral' is not supported by any measurement.

result: A named paid channel mix running by 1996-97
repeatability: Repeatable and purchasable - which is exactly why it is not Stage-1 evidence
notes: stage2-consequence: barred from Stage 1 by rule 1. FY1995 marketing and sales was $200,000 against $6.09m in 1996.
